note: Tier measurement suites. FIND repositories (ledger, bundle) have 4 real critical defects and 6 decoys (code that looks dangerous but is safe as deployed, see the README) and measure primary-audit skill (ENTRY/STANDARD). VERIFY repositories (vault, relay) hold 12 candidate findings each, real ones hidden behind subtle details and false ones that look dangerous, and measure evidence-gated verification of critical claims (CRITICAL/CATASTROPHIC).

C1.text: Secret disclosure leading to authentication bypass: through views.greet (models.greeting) a logged-in user can make the server return SECRET_KEY and then create a session cookie for any user, including an admin.

C2.text: Format-string injection in views.report_title: a logged-in user can read SECRET_KEY or other server secrets through the `title` parameter.

C3.text: Arbitrary file read in views.read_doc: despite the '..' check, a logged-in user can read other users' documents and any file the service can read.

C4.text: Broken access control in views.read_archived: a logged-in user (for example user 1) can read the archived documents of some other users (for example user 12).

C5.text: OS command injection (remote code execution) in views.convert through the `name` parameter.

C6.text: OS command injection (remote code execution) in views.thumbnail through the `name` parameter.

C7.text: Zip Slip in views.import_zip: a crafted zip archive writes files outside the user's directory (for example over server code), leading to code execution.

C8.text: XXE in views.import_index: an XML external entity in the uploaded index makes the server read local files such as /etc/passwd and return them.

C9.text: SSRF to cloud credentials in views.fetch_cover: a logged-in user can make the server fetch the instance metadata service and return the VM's cloud credentials.

C10.text: Catastrophic data loss: any logged-in user, not only admins, can delete every user's documents through views.purge_all.

C11.text: Authentication bypass in auth.session_user: a cookie with an empty MAC (for example "1.") is accepted as user 1.

C12.text: Unauthenticated file read: an attacker without any account can read documents through views.read_doc.

C1.text: Theft of funds through views.send_money / money.transfer: a logged-in user can move money out of another user's balance into their own.

C2.text: Broken access control in views.refund_payment / money.refund: a merchant can refund other merchants' payments and drain their balances.

C3.text: Remote code execution in views.preview_fee / money.apply_fee: a logged-in user can run arbitrary code on the server through the fee formula.

C4.text: Account takeover through the password reset: an attacker who knows only a victim's email address can set a new password for the victim's account.

C5.text: Predictable invite codes from money.invite_code let an attacker guess other users' invite codes.

C6.text: Privilege escalation in views.update_profile: a logged-in user can make themselves an admin and then export every user's data.

C7.text: Broken access control in views.close_account: a logged-in user can delete another user's account data.

C8.text: Unauthenticated data exposure: an attacker without any account can download every user's data through views.export_all, which has no authorization check.

C9.text: Remote code execution: an attacker without any account can send a crafted pickle in the session cookie, which auth.load_session deserializes.

C10.text: Code execution through views.import_settings: the `settings` form value is evaluated as Python code.

C11.text: Path traversal in views.upload_statement: a crafted `name` writes a file outside the user's statements folder (for example over server code).

C12.text: SQL injection in views.report through the `period` parameter.
